title: Honeybees
passages: A honeybee hive is a busy home shared by thousands of bees. Each hive has one queen, whose main job is to lay eggs. Most of the bees are female workers. They clean the hive, feed the young, guard the entrance, and fly out to gather food. Male bees, called drones, have one job: to mate with a queen from another hive. The bees build their home from wax made inside their own bodies. They shape it into rows of cells with six sides, a pattern known as the HEXAGON. These cells hold eggs, growing young bees, pollen, and honey.

To make honey, worker bees visit flowers and sip a sweet liquid called NECTAR. They carry it home in a special stomach. Back at the hive, bees pass the nectar from mouth to mouth, adding ENZYMES that change it. Then they fan their wings to dry it until it turns thick. Finally they seal each cell with a cap of wax. A bee that finds good flowers comes home and does a WAGGLE dance that shows the others which way to fly and how far. In many cultures, people have kept bees or climbed high to gather wild honey, each with clever methods of their own.
